newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli cabinet votes further structural changes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli cabinet votes further structural changes.

text.p: Israel's cabinet approved five more measures designed to make the public sector more efficient and agreed to study a proposal to sell public housing to tenants, the Treasury said on Wednesday.
The measures are part of a package of 25 which the Treasury brought to the cabinet for approval on January 8 to try to enhance competition and public sector efficiency.
Most of the major elements, such as a limited opening of public transport to competition and lowering the retirement age, were approved in the first cabinet meeting.
The measures approved today include reducing municipal tax exemptions, increasing water rates and taxes and privatising the eight public sector housing management companies.

The cabinet also agreed to consider a proposal by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that the homes themselves be sold to tenants. A committee was set up to study the issue and report back within six months.

Two measures originally proposed by the Treasury remain outstanding. One is a change in water-usage regulations and the other is an increase in the amount of land tendered by the state for housing construction.
Another proposal, to increase the amount of land in inventory ready for tendering, is being studied by a committee after it ran into opposition from Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon.
